subject: provider-only-admission-leftover.v1

verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory. Advisories do not block.
acceptanceGrade: ACCEPT-WITH-ONE-ADVISORY. Application-grade for what this artifact is — a measurement of two leftover classes plus a candidate obligation — and expressly not a closure.

scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsAccepted: That NT-3 and NT-5 are hostile-but-well-formed host-admission classes; that no live gate corpus exercises them, with G21, G20 and G10 each ruled out on its own quoted terms; that the two v3 class texts are reproduced exactly; and that one later DR-G* obligation with the proposed owner, claim and corpus would be the shape that owns them.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatIsNotAccepted: This ACCEPT does not close DR-133's leftover-design, does not add DR-G23 or any gate row, does not change required-now 18, and does not make DR-133 eligible or SATISFIED. The artifact says all of this itself. NT-3 and NT-5 remain leftover-design until a later act adds the row.
scopeOfThisAcceptance.whatItUnblocks: A later D-000 act that adds the proposed row. That act is simultaneously an MF-6 file-08 write, a D-002 required-gate-set change and a D-086 successor, which the artifact names as three limbs rather than one — the correct characterisation.

advisories.title: The 19-of-19 forward statement holds only if the later act records the identifier at the same time it adds the row; adding the row alone would drop condition 4 from MET
advisories.finding: requiredNowEffectIfAdoptedLater reads: 'If a later MF-6 adds this row to the required-now set, D-086 required-now cardinality becomes 19 of 19.' Live file 08's condition-4 row is MET, and it is MET because the measured cell reads '18 of 18 required gates name a recorded identifier'. A nineteenth required row that is added without a recorded identifier would make that 18 of 19 and would flip condition 4 from MET to not MET — a readiness regression on a currently-MET condition. The statement is not wrong: the proposal bundles namedHarnessDraft alongside the row, so an act adopting this proposal whole would record the identifier and reach 19 of 19. But the precondition is doing real work and is nowhere stated, and the trap is not obvious to a drafter reading only the cardinality sentence.
advisories.whyNotShouldFix: Nothing asserted is false, the statement is explicitly conditional and scoped to a later act which the artifact declines to perform, and the identifier the precondition needs is in the same proposedObligation object. The artifact also volunteers the cardinality consequence at all, which it was not obliged to do.
advisories.repair: One clause: the later act must add the row and record its named identifier in the same act, since adding a nineteenth required gate without a recorded name would move condition 4 from MET to not MET.

independence.priorParticipation: The finding that NT-3 and NT-5 do not ride any live gate corpus is mine, from the join v5 cycle, and this artifact is built on it. So the risk is accepting my own conclusion restated back to me. I re-derived the exclusions from the live gate rows rather than from my earlier verdicts, re-compared both class texts against the contract byte for byte, and searched the DR-G20 row in full for the Coverage claim rather than trusting either the artifact or my memory.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with one advisory. Thirteen attacks run, one landed and it is advisory-grade. Read the scope before recording: this is a measurement plus a candidate obligation, not a closure. DR-133's leftover-design stays open for NT-3 and NT-5, no gate row is added, required-now stays 18, and the row stays OPEN and not SATISFIED — the artifact says every one of those itself, and the token SATISFIED does not appear in it at all. Custody is clean: eae27692 at 0444 unmoved, dispatch and prompt agreeing, HEAD never left 95bab60, file 08 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree, all four cited digests reproducing, and D-145 verified as ADOPTED in live COORD with my turn-2 verdict pinned. The substance holds under every check I could put to it. Both class texts are reproduced from the v3 contract byte for byte, six of six fields. The three exclusions rest on the gates' own quoted terms and I re-derived each from the live rows rather than from my earlier verdicts: G21's corpus really is the crash-through-recovery fault list and its candidate discard really is post-fault leak prevention; G10's claim really is opacity, one-shotness and fate-compatibility; and for the one negative claim that could have been sloppy — that G20 says nothing about Coverage-domain sufficiency — I searched the whole DR-G20 row and the string Coverage does not occur in it. The proposed obligation is well formed: candidate-not-adopted, with an owner, a claim scoped precisely to hostile-but-well-formed provider admission, a named-harness draft marked not authored and not QUALIFIED, and one corpus entry per class. DR-G23 does not exist in file 08, whose gate table runs to DR-G22, and the artifact anticipates a later collision with a remint clause. It also characterises the later act correctly as three limbs at once — an MF-6 file-08 write, a D-002 required-gate-set change and a D-086 successor — rather than flattening it to one. One obligation for two classes does not repeat the over-bundling that sank join v1, because both classes are the same kind and the claim says so. The advisory is that the 19-of-19 cardinality statement holds only if the later act records the identifier in the same act that adds the row: file 08's condition 4 is MET because 18 of 18 required gates name a recorded identifier, so a nineteenth required row added without a name would flip condition 4 from MET to not MET. The proposal does bundle the identifier, so nothing here is false — but the precondition is doing real work and is worth one clause, because the trap is invisible to a drafter reading only the cardinality sentence.
